# Pure Python cubic polynomial regression using stable QR decomposition

def qr_decomposition(A):
    """Compute QR decomposition using Gram-Schmidt"""
    m, n = A.shape
    Q = [[0]*n for _ in range(m)]
    R = [[0]*n for _ in range(n)]
    
    for j in range(n):
        v = [A[i][j] for i in range(m)]
        for i in range(j):
            R[i][j] = sum(Q[k][i] * A[k][j] for k in range(m))
            for k in range(m):
                v[k] -= R[i][j] * Q[k][i]
        
        R[j][j] = sum(v[k]**2 for k in range(m)) ** 0.5
        if R[j][j] < 1e-12:
            R[j][j] = 1e-12
            
        for k in range(m):
            Q[k][j] = v[k] / R[j][j]
    
    return Q, R

def solve_qr(Q, R, b):
    """Solve least squares using QR"""
    n = len(R)
    # Qt * b
    Qtb = [sum(Q[k][i] * b[k] for k in range(len(Q))) for i in range(n)]
    
    # Back substitution
    x = [0] * n
    for i in range(n-1, -1, -1):
        if abs(R[i][i]) < 1e-12:
            x[i] = 0
        else:
            x[i] = Qtb[i]
            for j in range(i+1, n):
                x[i] -= R[i][j] * x[j]
            x[i] /= R[i][i]
    return x
